articles.title: Early-life pain led to lasting social deficits in mice, and brain stimulation reversed them
articles.summary: Early-life pain may leave a lasting mark on social behavior by tipping the balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain. In mice, restoring that balance, including with deep brain stimulation, reversed the resulting social deficits.

articles.title: College students who use more cannabis are less willing to share it, and less likely to use it with friends

articles.title: Online meat-shaming may do little to change minds, new research suggests

articles.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable

articles.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene

articles.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques

articles.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
